correctness.rationale: The Shapley degree/2 identity follows from edge OR unanimity-sharing, the inclusion-area/first-cover equation counts each edge exactly n-c+1 times, and the disjoint-clique iff follows from a feasible sorted merge of a fixed marginal-gain multiset. For kK3 disjoint union qK2 the original-degree restriction introduces precisely kq zero-before-one inversions, producing the exact optimum and limiting ratio. The finite universal threshold is exhaustively verified for every one of 1099 labeled graphs of order <=5, by independent full-permutation and subset-DP implementations in verify_coverage.py. The infinite family is proved analytically, not inferred from finite tests.

evidence: The unrestricted nullspace-perturbation ranking theorem of Li et al. does not preserve the unit-positive edge-feature representation and cannot yield a 5-vertex minimality statement about it.

The generic subset recurrence of Biniaz et al. computes optimal cover time for arbitrary graphs but has no Shapley-restriction theorem, whereas this claim compares two objective optima with a sharp count and exact all-parameter gap.

The known complete multipartite minimum formula does not imply the minimum formula for the complementary union of cliques; the sum of cover-time costs of complementary graphs is constant at each ordering, exchanging min with max.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The same-object comparison identifies both the graph-coverage representation and the inclusion-area objective. The new result is neither the general MSVC equivalence nor a restatement of unrestricted Shapley ranking failure; it supplies an exact structural criterion and earliest restricted obstruction with an asymptotically nonzero loss. Related directed-network trust-game and voting-game Shapley formulas address other characteristic functions and do not imply this restricted AUC result.

evidence: For an edge-OR coverage game the Shapley score of a player is half its incident-edge degree, while inclusion area is (n+1)|E| minus the total first-cover time of the edges.
Biniaz et al., arXiv:2609.27117, Appendix A.1, prove a general exact subset recurrence for minimum-sum vertex cover, but do not impose the original-degree Shapley ranking constraint.

The published complete-multipartite exact-value result minimizes first-cover time for a complete multipartite graph; a disjoint clique union is its complement, and the constant-sum relation switches minimization on the original to maximization on the complement.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The cover-time equivalence is made explicit, and is not claimed as new. General exact algorithms permit computational evaluation of an instance, but do not state the restricted attribution theorem: the only five-player unweighted graph-coverage obstruction, an iff for clique unions, and the exact tie-resistant loss. Complementing a graph changes minimizing cover time into maximizing it on the complement; the closest complete-multipartite minimum result therefore does not dominate the new claim.

value.rationale: The limitation of Shapley-based player ranking is central to inclusion-AUC attribution. This theorem demonstrates a sharp restriction effect: arbitrary cooperative games already admit failures at four players, but unweighted monotone submodular graph coverage games are protected through four and have one unique five-player obstruction. The complete clique-union iff and the exact kq penalty show that tie-breaking cannot repair the mismatch and the relative loss can persist asymptotically (up to 1/(7+sqrt(39)) within the explicit family). These facts respond to the meaningful question whether bad rankings require pathological unrestricted utility functions, not merely an arbitrary finite enumeration.
